public_notes.title: Community Continuity And Reorganization
public_notes.text: The Tribe's history, updated December 31, 2022, describes families maintaining community in Southampton County through land loss and racial reclassification. It recounts family clusters coming together to reorganize in February 2002, followed by an elected Tribal Government in May. In this account, reorganization is a new phase in a continuing community's history. It does not mean that Cheroenhaka people first existed in 2002, and it does not merge this Tribe with the separate Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia.

public_notes.title: Language Records And Public Learning
public_notes.text: The Tribe's language page brings together vocabulary records it dates to 1820 and the 1830s, alongside correspondence about the language's Iroquoian relationships. The Cattashowrock Town page connects that history to a public interpretation site, with trails labelled in Iroquoian and English. These are the Tribe's accounts of its records and educational work. They do not establish today's number of speakers, class schedules, visitor opening times or measured learning outcomes.

public_notes.title: Treaties, Land And Family Continuity
public_notes.text: The Tribe's timeline describes treaties with colonial Virginia, a reservation and leaders working to preserve land, language and community as colonial policy changed. It also describes Nottoway families sustaining genealogy, oral tradition and community ties through pressures to assimilate during the Racial Integrity Act era. This is its published historical account, not a present boundary or treaty-rights determination.

public_notes.title: Community History And Education
public_notes.text: The Tribe dates the opening of its Capron Community House & Interpretive Center to May 5, 2012. Its page says Nottoway family citizens operate and fund it and that community and tribal volunteers staff it. The exhibit connects trade, colonial expansion and continuing tribal identity. These are the Tribe's descriptions of community education, not independent confirmation of today's staffing, hours or class availability.
